sentences.text:
Vikas vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko. ... on 17
January, 2024
Author: Pankaj Bhatia

Bench: Pankaj Bhatia
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc-Lko:4964
Court No. - 12
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 9930 of 2023
Applicant :- Vikas

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

And 3 Others Counsel for Applicant :- Farooq Ayoob Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
None appears on behalf of the informant despite notice.

2. Initially a missing person report was lodged, however in the statement recorded under Section 161 & 164 Cr.P.C., the victim did not support the case of the prosecution and stated that both of them had married.
The counsel for the applicant has filed supplementary affidavit disclosing that during trial the victim has turned hostile.
There is no document on record as prescribed in the Rules framed under the Juvenile Justice Act to determine the age of the victim, which shall be done at the time of trial.
Vikas vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

entities.text: Vikas vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. Learned A.G.A. opposed the bail prayer.

4. Considering the said two statements of the victim recorded under Section 161 & 164 Cr.P.C.
coupled with the fact that during trial the victim has turned hostile, the applicant has no criminal history and is in custody since 22.06.2023 and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.

Accordingly,
the bail application is allowed.

5. Let the applicant Vikas be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No. 0143 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC and Section 5/6 POCSO Act, Police Station Kursi, District Barabanki, on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 17.1.2024 Arun  Vikas vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko. ... on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20343508/
